textReplacer.subtitle: Free Text Replacer for find and replace, including turning \n into line breaks.
textReplacer.hintLiteral: Find is literal by default, so \n matches a backslash plus n. With interpret-replace on, \n in Replace becomes a real line break.
textReplacer.hintRegexGreedy: Find is a JavaScript regular expression. Quantifiers like .* match as much as possible. Uncheck Greedy matching to take the shortest match. Replacement supports $1, $2, and $&.
textReplacer.hintRegexLazy: Greedy matching is off, so * + ? and {n,m} match as little as possible (same as writing .*? or +?). Replacement supports $1, $2, and $&.
textReplacer.placeholder: Paste text that contains \n or other characters to replace…
textReplacer.intro: Use this Text Replacer to find and replace text without leaving the browser. Paste source on the left, set Find and Replace, and the result updates as you type. Copy or download the output; nothing is uploaded.
textReplacer.newlineBody: Text copied from JSON, logs, or chat often shows \n as two characters. The default replace turns those into real line breaks.
textReplacer.liveBody: The right pane updates as you edit Find and Replace, and shows how many replacements were made.
textReplacer.privateBody: Open a local file in Text Replacer, copy the result, or download a .txt file without uploading anything.

faqs.question: How do I turn \n into real line breaks in Text Replacer?
faqs.answer: In Text Replacer, keep Find as \n and Replace as \n, with “Interpret escapes in replace” turned on. Find stays literal, so it matches the two characters backslash and n. Replace then inserts a real newline.

faqs.question: What escape sequences work in Text Replacer?
faqs.answer: With interpret-replace enabled, \n becomes a newline, \t a tab, \r a carriage return, and \\ a backslash.

faqs.question: Does Text Replacer upload my text?
faqs.answer: No. Text Replacer runs find, replace, and preview in your browser.

faqs.question: When should I use regex in Text Replacer?
faqs.answer: Turn on Use regex in Text Replacer to treat Find as a JavaScript regular expression. For example, Find (\d+) and Replace [$1] wraps each number in brackets. Greedy matching (the default) lets .* consume as much as possible; uncheck it to match the shortest span instead. In regex mode, \n matches a real newline; to match the two characters backslash and n, use \\n.

faqs.question: Is Text Replacer free?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is free to use in the browser, with no account required.
